character.description: front-facing original Pixel Night Shift build engineer with amber work helmet, coral-orange armor, deep navy structure, pale metal accents, broad planted silhouette, and one connected heavy industrial tool; preserve exact locked identity

idle.action: strict low-amplitude four-phase planted idle loop: frame 1 neutral, frame 2 a tiny inhale visible only as an approximately one-logical-pixel helmet/shoulder rise, frame 3 a tiny exhale, frame 4 a near-neutral return that flows quietly to frame 1. Lock both boot silhouettes, leg spacing, pelvis center, overall scale, and the heavy tool's horizontal angle, height, side, and two-hand connection across all four frames; do not lift, rotate, or swing the tool during idle. Target consecutive alpha IoU 0.93-0.98 and final-to-first at least 0.95, with small nonzero changes rather than duplicate holds; foot-centroid drift must stay below 0.5 logical pixel

upgrade.action: brief build upgrade acknowledgement with clear start-middle-end poses: frame 1 near idle, frame 2 braces and lifts the same connected heavy tool to a modest diagonal, frame 3 reaches the peak lift without covering the helmet, frame 4 settles near the starting pose. Lock both boot silhouettes, foot spacing, pelvis center, character scale, and front-facing torso across every frame; never widen the stance, translate the body, or rotate to a side view. Keep the exact same tool shape and two-hand connection; foot-centroid drift must stay below 0.75 logical pixel. No detached sparks, glow, particles, or extra equipment

style: match the attached canonical Base Lock image EXACTLY: same 38px raw pixel pitch resolving to an approximately 25-logical-pixel-tall character, same broad proportions, outline weight, amber/coral/navy/pale-metal palette, shading density, helmet identity, and connected heavy tool. Do not restyle, change proportions, or add/remove detail density. Avoid polished illustration, painterly rendering, anime key art, 3D render, vector polish, glossy lighting, soft gradients, anti-aliased high-detail edges, and dense micro-pixels.

qa.min_used_pixels_basis: The shipped 32x32 build_engineer contains 400 opaque pixels. Area calibration at logical height 26 gives 400 * (26 / 32)^2 = 264.06 expected pixels; 250 is a strict 94.7% floor while allowing the requested breathing/tool motion.
